tasks.notes: fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs: `bootAsync` drops the `timeout: 60000` that `boot` has carried since BASE. Every merge-sim leg now runs its boot through `bootAsync`/`gatedBoot`, so a boot that wedges (a stub that never writes the file a `sleep 0.1` loop polls, a poll that never terminates) no longer gets killed at 60 s and reported as that leg's failure — the sim hangs until tests/test_fleet_suite.py's MJS_TIMEOUT=300 kills the whole file, and the run reports a timed-out sim with no `ok (`/`FAIL —` line naming the culprit. `child_process.spawn` accepts the same `timeout` option, so parity is one line and keeps the promise's documented claim of 'the same command, the same environment and a result of the same shape'. Not blocking: M1's evidence shows the sim finishing in 13 s, so nothing wedges on the tree as patched.; unverified: the rig change (`runTests` is now `async` and awaits each case) reaches all eight sims that import it, but the driver's evidence exercises only two — test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs and test_sandbox_boot_approved.mjs (M7's chosen synchronous sibling). The six other rig users — test_sandbox_boot.mjs, _edges, _record, _approval_evidence, _effort, _selfmerge — were exactly what the deleted leg (j) loop used to run inside this file, so this diff removes the only in-tree evidence they take the new runner. Reading them at BASE, each ends with `runTests(tests)` as its last statement and registers only synchronous cases, so the await-per-case change is behaviour-preserving for them and the risk is low; the acceptance mode is `suite`, which is where that sentence now lives. What would settle it: a run of `pytest tests/test_fleet_suite.py` (or `node` on those six paths) on this tree.; fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs: the WIDTH comment says it is 'How many boots are in flight at once, and the only knob this file's wall turns on', but the gate only wraps `gatedBoot`; the green scenario reaches the script through the rig's `greenAsync`, which calls `bootAsync` directly and never takes a slot. The sim therefore runs up to WIDTH + 1 = 4 boots at once, which is the whole of a four-vCPU sandbox the comment sizes WIDTH against. Either route green through the gate too (`greenAsync` cannot, since the gate is the sim's — so boot green as a local `scenario()` and drop the `greenAsync as green` import) or soften the comment to say WIDTH bounds the scenarios and the rig's memoised green boot sits beside them.; tests/test_fleet_suite.py: the new comment opens with seven walls in descending order ('40.9 s, 33.3 s, 30.7 s, 17.0 s, 13.3 s, 12.6 s, 10.6 s') directly above a SLOW_FIRST that is deliberately NOT in that order — the prose then says test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs, the 40.9 s entry, follows the 33.3 s selfmerge sim. A reader can no longer map a number to a name, which is the one thing the number line is for, and the next person to re-measure has to guess the pairing. Suggest annotating each wall with its sim (e.g. 'proof_runs 40.9 s, selfmerge 33.3 s, boot 30.7 s, merge 17.0 s, edges 13.3 s, exam_evidence 12.6 s, publish_fold 10.6 s') so the divergence from longest-first, which M6 forces by pinning SLOW_FIRST[0], reads as deliberate rather than as drift.; `bootAsync` drops the 60 s watchdog that `boot` keeps. `boot` (fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:659-666) passes `timeout: 60000` to `spawnSync`, so a wedged boot is killed and comes back as a failing leg with a signal; `bootAsync` (fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:685-697) passes only `env` and `stdio`, so a boot that hangs never settles — every leg awaiting it, and the whole sim, hangs until the suite's MJS_TIMEOUT=300 kills the process with no attribution (and forever when the sim is run standalone outside `timeout 60`). The doc comment promises the same result shape as `boot` but is silent about the missing cap. `node:child_process.spawn` accepts `timeout`/`killSignal` and reports the kill on 'close' as `(null, 'SIGTERM')`, which is exactly the shape `boot`'s timeout produces, so parity costs one line.; unverified: the SLOW_FIRST rewrite goes past what the task asks and no exam checks it. M6 pins only `SLOW_FIRST[0] == 'test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs'`, `MJS_TIMEOUT == 300`, the 'longest' comment and the three dead phrases; the Context adds only that the merge sim "moves down the list to where its new wall puts it". The diff instead replaces four of the seven entries (tests/test_fleet_suite.py:19-22): `test_run_engine_examiner.mjs` — the 83.5 s number two in the BASE comment, and still present in fleet/tests/ — plus `test_exam_edited_patches.mjs`, `test_run_engine_integrated_runs.mjs` and `test_deadline_slack.mjs` drop out, and `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs` moves from a measured 8.1 s to a claimed 40.9 s (tests/test_fleet_suite.py:5-6). Those walls are a fresh measurement no Run: command reproduces, and the wall numbers in the new comment (selfmerge ~33 s, boot ~31 s) also disagree with the plan's own Context figures (66.1 s and 61.2 s). If a number is off, a genuinely long sim now goes out late under `--dist load` and strands a worker — the exact failure the list exists to prevent. Settled by re-timing the suite under `-n 6` on the box the comment names and either restoring `test_run_engine_examiner.mjs` or saying in the comment why it fell out.; unverified: the now-async `runTests` (fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:941) is exercised on only one of its eight callers on this tree. The change is sanctioned by the task (M7's grep allows `export async function runTests(`) and the seven siblings all end with `runTests(tests)` as their last statement, so registration order and `process.exit(1)` behaviour are preserved on inspection; M7's evidence runs `test_sandbox_boot_approved.mjs` green. But leg (j)'s nested loop, which used to run `test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, `_edges`, `_record`, `_approval_evidence`, `_effort` and `_selfmerge` against the rig, is deleted in this same diff, so nothing in this submission's evidence covers those six against the new runner — the acceptance mode ('suite') is what has to catch a regression there. Settled by the committed suite running fleet/tests/test_*.mjs on this tree.; concern: measurement-vs-exam: M6 pins SLOW_FIRST[0] to test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs, but measured wall under `-n 6` on this box makes test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs (40.9 s) longer than selfmerge (33.3 s). I satisfied M6 and kept the comments truthful: selfmerge is named as the longest sim that boots sandbox-boot.sh (the pole the merge sim used to hide), with proof_runs named as the longest sim of any kind and placed second. The comment explains that the head of the list is dispatched in one round, so order within it is not load-bearing.; concern: SLOW_FIRST membership was also refreshed to the seven measured-longest sims (dropping test_run_engine_examiner.mjs, test_exam_edited_patches.mjs, test_run_engine_integrated_runs.mjs, test_deadline_slack.mjs — all now under 5 s, deadline_slack 0.0 s — and adding edges, exam_evidence, publish_fold). Only [0] is pinned by M6; this is dispatch order only and changes no assertion.

completenessFindings.detail: fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs:941 — task 1's rig change turns the existing export `runTests` from a synchronous function into `export async function runTests(tests)` (awaiting each `fn()`), which is the one place the rig grew *through* a BASE export rather than beside it (the plan's Global Constraint phrases it as "the rig grows beside its BASE exports rather than through them"; its own gloss — "what a sibling sim imports today keeps its meaning, and a sibling that registers only synchronous tests is not asked to change" — does hold, and Machine clause M7 explicitly admits `export (async )?function runTests(`). Behaviourally the seven sibling sims are unaffected: each calls `runTests(tests)` as the module's final statement (test_sandbox_boot.mjs:1065, _edges:824, _record:313, _approved:201, _approval_evidence:558, _effort:118, _selfmerge:748), registration order, the `ok (` lines and the `process.exit(1)` path are unchanged, and the driver's suite is green. The residue worth an issue rather than a stop: those seven call sites now discard a promise, so a throw from the post-loop tail of `runTests` (the `fs.rmSync(tmpRoot, …)` at :954) would surface as an unhandled rejection instead of a synchronous throw — same non-zero exit under Node 22 today, but a new seam nobody's call site handles.
